Insertion pain, bleeding, expulsion, uterine perforation, insertion-related PID, and rare pregnancy despite the device (intrauterine or ectopic — both serious).

💊Combined Hormonal Contraception: Mechanism & Regimens10 items▾

Recall
How does combined hormonal contraception prevent pregnancy?
tap to flip
Answer
Suppresses FSH and LH → no dominant follicle and no LH surge → no ovulation. The progestin also thickens cervical mucus and produces a thin/decidualized endometrium.
Recall
CHC: which hormone suppresses which gonadotropin?
tap to flip
Answer
Estrogen primarily suppresses FSH; progestin primarily suppresses LH (and thickens cervical mucus).
Board trap · Withdrawal bleed is not a periodBleeding in the hormone-free interval is not a normal endogenous menstrual cycle — it occurs because exogenous steroid exposure stops, not because of ovulatory cycling.
  • ✎Modern combined pills usually contain about µg ethinyl estradiol; high-dose formulations are about µg.
Pill, patch and ring — same mechanism, same contraindications
MethodScheduleMethod-specific side effectsAnswer
Combined pillTraditional 21 active days + 7 hormone-free days; 24/4, extended-cycle and continuous regimens also existNausea, breakthrough bleeding, headache; VTE
Transdermal patchOne patch weekly for 3 weeks, then 1 week off; delivers estrogen/progestin through skinSkin irritation; estrogen/VTE effects — higher average estrogen exposure than a standard 35-µg pill
Vaginal ringIn place 3 weeks (continuous vaginal release), removed for a 1-week hormone-free interval in cyclic useVaginal discharge, headache, vaginitis
  • ✎Patch efficacy is reduced in women weighing more than .
  • ✎Vaginal ring removed during intercourse: replace within hours.
Recall
Who is an appropriate CHC candidate?
tap to flip
Answer
A healthy patient without estrogen-related thrombotic/vascular contraindications who can adhere to daily (pill), weekly (patch) or monthly (ring) dosing.
Recall
Common non-serious CHC side effects?
tap to flip
Answer
Nausea, headache, breakthrough bleeding and perceived weight change.
Recall
Fertility after stopping CHC?
tap to flip
Answer
Generally returns; no specific interpregnancy delay is required.

Coronary artery disease / cerebrovascular accident (stroke)—
Smoking at age ≥35 years≥15 cigarettes/day = MEC 4; fewer than 15/day = MEC 3: ↑ MI, stroke, DVT and PE

  • ✎No combined OCP (screen before initiation) for a woman aged years or older who smokes cigarettes/day (MEC 4); at the same age, fewer than 15 cigarettes/day is MEC .
  • ✎CHC becomes increasingly inappropriate as BP severity/vascular disease increases: systolic BP ≥ or diastolic BP ≥ mm Hg, before or while using = MEC category — do not use (a woman with BP 168/104 requesting the combined pill is not prescribed it).
Recall
Classic-textbook RELATIVE contraindications to CHC (11)?
tap to flip
Answer
Uterine fibroids, lactation, diabetes mellitus, sickle-cell disease, hepatic disease, hypertension, SLE, age ≥40 with vascular risk, migraine headaches, seizure disorder, elective surgery.
This list is cruder than current MEC, which grades each condition separately.
Board trap · The classic 'relative' list vs MECTempting: treat every item on the classic relative list as a mild caution. Right (US MEC 2024): migraine with aura, severe hypertension, SLE with positive/unknown antiphospholipid antibodies, and major surgery with prolonged immobilization are MEC 4 — do not use; controlled or milder hypertension = 3; diabetes = 2 if uncomplicated but 3/4 with nephropathy, retinopathy, neuropathy, other vascular disease or duration >20 years; migraine without aura = 2; uterine fibroids and epilepsy = 1 (but enzyme-inducing anticonvulsants make CHC category 3); lactation depends on time since delivery. Sickle-cell disease: MEC 4 in US MEC 2024, category 2 in WHO MEC 2015.

SSmoking at age ≥35
LLiver or major vascular disease
Any one present → choose a non-estrogen method according to MEC.

Screening before prescribing CHC?
tap to flip
Answer
Measure BP and screen for VTE, migraine, smoking, liver and cancer risks.

🟡Progestin-Only Methods: POP & Implant9 items▾

Recall
Class mechanism of progestin-only contraception?
tap to flip
Answer
Thickens cervical mucus, inhibits sperm transport, thins/atrophies the endometrium and variably suppresses ovulation.
Progestin-only methods compared
MethodOvulation suppressionAdverse effectsMajor concernAnswer
POP (norethindrone)Only about 50% of cycles (mucus + endometrial atrophy ± ovulation suppression)Irregular bleeding, follicular cysts, acne, breast tenderness, irritabilityCurrent breast cancer is a major progestin concern
DMPAMore consistent; also reduces tubal motility and acts on mucus/endometriumIrregular bleeding, weight gain, BMD loss, delayed return to fertilityMethod-specific MEC conditions; the estrogen issue does not apply
Etonogestrel implantSuppresses ovulation; continuous progestin exposure without daily adherence — a highly effective progestin-only optionIrregular bleeding, headacheCurrent breast cancer
  • ✎Traditional POP: norethindrone mg daily (norgestrel 0.075 mg behaves the same), which suppresses ovulation in only about % of cycles — so precise daily timing is critical.
  • ✎POP must be taken at the same time every day: for norethindrone/norgestrel a delay of more than hours counts as a missed pill (late/missed pills are why typical-use failure is high). Newer POPs are more forgiving — desogestrel 75 µg hours, drospirenone 4 mg hours (CDC 2024 / product labelling).
Recall
Why do progestin-only methods suit women who cannot take CHC — and which patients?
tap to flip
Answer
They avoid estrogen-mediated increases in coagulation. Favored for migraine with aura, hypertension, smokers aged ≥35 years, CAD, or a personal history of thromboembolism; POP is also appropriate in breastfeeding.
Recall
Why is bleeding irregular on progestin-only methods?
tap to flip
Answer
Endometrial proliferation is suppressed unevenly.
  • ✎Etonogestrel implant (Nexplanon): inserted subdermally in the ; approved for up to years of contraception (FDA labelling, January 2026) with no user action until removal/replacement. Classic textbook and earlier labelling: 3 years.
Recall
Commonest reason for discontinuing the implant?
tap to flip
Answer
Irregular bleeding (common) — though most of the bleeding is lighter than a normal period.
  • ★Method-related bleeding — POP, DMPA, implant, IUD, CHC — is classified under iatrogenic causes of abnormal uterine bleeding, after pathology is excluded.

💉DMPA (Depot Medroxyprogesterone Acetate)6 items▾

  • ✎DMPA dose: mg IM every 3 months (standard) or mg SC every 3 months.
  • ✎DMPA suppresses ovulation for about weeks, giving roughly a -week grace period beyond the usual 12-week schedule.
🧠 Memory toolCounsel before the first DMPA injection — 4 B's
BBleeding — irregular early, later amenorrhea
BBody weight change
BBone-density loss (reversible)
BBaby delayed — slow return to fertility

DMPA and bone
QuestionAnswerAnswer
Why does BMD fall?Ovarian estradiol is suppressed
When is loss fastest?Most rapid in the first year (greatest early in use); increases with duration of use

⏰Emergency Contraception16 items▾

Recall
Emergency contraception — when is it used?
tap to flip
Answer
After unprotected intercourse but before an established pregnancy is recognized.
Recall
Indications for EC?
tap to flip
Answer
Unprotected intercourse, condom breakage, missed pills, ring/patch displacement, IUD expulsion, or a late DMPA injection.
Emergency contraception options
OptionDose & windowMechanismRoleAnswer
Levonorgestrel1.5 mg PO once, as soon as possible; labelled for ≤72 h, may be used up to 120 h but efficacy falls with delayPrimarily delays/inhibits ovulationMost widely available oral EC; fewer estrogen-related adverse effects than older combined regimens. Less effective than ulipristal at 72–120 h and possibly in obesity (CDC 2024). Classic textbook: first-line oral EC
Ulipristal acetate30 mg PO once ≤120 h / 5 daysSelective progesterone-receptor modulator — delays follicular ruptureMost effective oral EC — better than levonorgestrel, especially in the 72–120 h interval (CDC 2024, WHO 2021); delay starting hormonal contraception for 5 days after it
Copper IUDInsert ≤120 h / 5 days after unprotected intercourseLocal inflammatory environment hostile to sperm/fertilizationMost effective EC overall, if eligible for IUD insertion and ongoing contraception is desired
Combined estrogen-progestin (Yuzpe) regimenEthinyl estradiol 100 µg + levonorgestrel 0.5 mg, 2 doses 12 h apart, within 120 h (WHO 2021)Delays/inhibits ovulationLeast preferred: more nausea/vomiting and lower efficacy than levonorgestrel-only. Philippines: no dedicated EC pill is registered (levonorgestrel EC was delisted in 2001), so DOH practice is this regimen using ordinary combined pills
  • ★EC by time since intercourse: establish time since intercourse and whether pregnancy is already known → ≤72 h: oral levonorgestrel or ulipristal → 72–120 h: ulipristal is the preferred pill (copper IUD remains most effective) → ≤120 h and IUD-eligible: copper IUD + continued long-term contraception → known established pregnancy: oral EC will not terminate it and copper-IUD EC is not inserted → after oral EC: start/continue an ongoing method and advise a pregnancy test if the expected menses is delayed.
🧠 Memory toolEC time windows — 3 days vs 5 days
72 hLevonorgestrel 1.5 mg — labelled window (earlier is better; weaker out to 120 h)
120 hUlipristal 30 mg — the better pill on days 3–5
120 hCopper IUD — most effective
  • ✎Copper-IUD EC is more than effective (WHO 2021): failure about 0.1% — roughly pregnancy per 1,000 users.
  • ✎Oral EC used within 72 hours fails in about .
Board trap · EC is not an abortifacientOral EC delays/suppresses ovulation and interferes with fertilization/tubal transport: it prevents pregnancy and does not terminate an implanted pregnancy. It is not intended for a known established pregnancy, but there is no evidence of fetal harm if levonorgestrel-type EC is taken inadvertently during one.
Recall
Pregnancy testing before EC — for which options?
tap to flip
Answer
Required before copper-IUD EC placement; recommended before ulipristal.
Board trap · Ulipristal in pregnancy and breastfeedingTempting: “ulipristal is unsuitable in breastfeeding” (classic textbook, antiprogestin concern). Right: breastfeeding is category 1 for ulipristal, levonorgestrel and copper-IUD EC (US MEC 2024); UK FSRH still advises expressing and discarding milk for 1 week after ulipristal. It remains not for use in a known pregnancy.
Recall
Does EC cover later intercourse in the same cycle?
tap to flip
Answer
No — oral EC is a single-event intervention, not long-term contraception; only a copper IUD left in place keeps protecting. Follow EC with counseling on a reliable ongoing method.
Recall
Next menses significantly delayed after EC → ?
tap to flip
Answer
Do a pregnancy test rather than repeatedly dosing EC.
Recall
Adverse effects of oral EC? Of copper-IUD EC?
tap to flip
Answer
Oral: nausea, vomiting, headache, dizziness, breast tenderness, transient bleeding changes. Copper IUD: the usual IUD risks — pain, heavier menses, perforation, expulsion, infection around insertion.
Recall
Does EC affect future fertility?
tap to flip
Answer
No — future fertility is not impaired by oral EC or by copper-IUD removal.
🩺 Think it through
Two women ask for emergency contraception: one had unprotected intercourse 48 hours ago, the other 4 days ago. What can each be offered?
48 h: oral levonorgestrel or ulipristal, or copper IUD — the copper IUD is more effective and continues as contraception. 4 days: ulipristal or copper IUD — both within 120 hours.
Recall
Woman with a history of DVT asks for emergency levonorgestrel → allowed?
tap to flip
Answer
Yes — CHC contraindications do not automatically prohibit one-time oral EC.

✂️Permanent Contraception: Tubal Sterilization & Vasectomy10 items▾

Tubal sterilization vs vasectomy
FeatureTubal sterilizationVasectomyAnswer
What is blockedConception needs the ovum to pass a patent fallopian tube → both tubes are occluded/divided so sperm and ovum cannot meetConception needs sperm to pass the vas deferens and the female reproductive tract → the vas is ligated/divided/occluded so sperm do not enter the ejaculate
Hormones afterwardsOvarian steroid production and menstrual hormonal cycles continue — the ovaries are not removedTestosterone production and sexual function intact — the testes remain hormonally functional
SettingPostpartum: small subumbilical incision under neuraxial anesthesia shortly after delivery (when consent and logistics are appropriate); or interval laparoscopyOffice procedure under local anesthesia; generally simpler, safer and less expensive than female sterilization
ComplicationsOperative: hemorrhage, infection, visceral/vascular injury, anesthesia complications, conversion to laparotomyUsually minor: bleeding, infection, local anesthetic/suture reactions; no major long-term systemic effects
Recall
Tubal sterilization techniques — postpartum vs interval?
tap to flip
Answer
Postpartum: Parkland / modified Pomeroy — ligates and removes a tubal segment. Interval laparoscopic: bipolar fulguration (coagulation), Falope rings, clips. Hysteroscopic tubal occlusion (Essure) is historical — withdrawn from the market (US sales ended 2018).
  • ✎Mortality from bilateral tubal ligation is about per 100,000 women.
Board trap · Vasectomy is NOT immediately effectiveResidual sperm remain distal to the occlusion. Continue another method until a semen analysis done no earlier than 8 weeks after the procedure (usually at 8–16 weeks; AUA) confirms azoospermia or only rare non-motile sperm (≤100,000/mL) — a man 2 weeks after vasectomy is not yet reliably sterile. Classic textbook: 6–8 weeks.
Recall
Pregnancy after tubal sterilization → first concern?
tap to flip
Answer
Ectopic pregnancy — tubal failure carries ectopic risk; confirm pregnancy location early.
  • ✎Sterilization regret is highest among women sterilized before age , regardless of parity.
  • ✎Counsel permanent contraception as essentially irreversible: tubal reversal is technically possible but unreliable, with success around depending on method.
Recall
Who is an appropriate candidate for permanent contraception — and who is not?
tap to flip
Answer
Patients/couples with completed desired family size, or for whom future pregnancy would pose unacceptable medical risk. Not for anyone with uncertain reproductive intent → choose LARC rather than irreversible sterilization.
Recall
What should be offered before female sterilization?
tap to flip
Answer
Counsel on LARC and vasectomy — similarly high efficacy without permanent female surgery.
Recall
When should sterilization counseling and consent take place?
tap to flip
Answer
Begin during pregnancy rather than waiting until immediately after delivery; postpartum sterilization should ideally be consented and planned before labor, then performed after delivery when previously chosen.

👶Postpartum & Breastfeeding Contraception6 items▾

  • ★Postpartum family-planning algorithm: ask the reproductive goal antenatally (spacing vs no further pregnancies) → immediately postpartum determine breastfeeding status + VTE risk + desire for LARC/permanent contraception → breastfeeding/early postpartum: favor progestin-only or LARC over estrogen → wants highly effective reversible: IUD or implant → wants nonhormonal highly effective: copper IUD → wants permanent: counsel tubal sterilization vs vasectomy, permanence, failure, regret and surgical risk → wants STI prevention: condom regardless of additional method → unsure about fertility plans: avoid permanent sterilization, choose reversible LARC.
Recall
When should postpartum contraception be discussed?
tap to flip
Answer
Antenatally — it need not wait for the 6-week visit; immediate postpartum contraception should be discussed before discharge.
Recall
Breastfeeding patient wants reliable contraception → preferred methods?
tap to flip
Answer
POP, DMPA, implant or LNG-IUD (an appropriate IUD) — progestin-only/LARC rather than estrogen-containing contraception.
Board trap · Estrogen in the early puerperiumAvoid/defer CHC while breastfeeding is being established and during the highest postpartum VTE-risk period: estrogen may decrease milk quantity/quality, and early postpartum estrogen increases VTE risk.
  • ✎CHC postpartum (US MEC 2024): not before days (MEC 4); days 21–42 = MEC 3 with VTE risk factors, 2 without (breastfeeding: 3 until day 30); after days no postpartum VTE restriction. WHO MEC 2015 is stricter for breastfeeding women: MEC 4 before weeks, 3 from 6 weeks to under 6 months, 2 from 6 months. Classic textbook: about 3 weeks, or 6 weeks if thrombotic risk or breastfeeding.
Board trap · Mother and fetus firstPostpartum contraception is addressed only after maternal/fetal stabilization: fetal compromise always takes precedence over contraceptive-procedure timing, and a persistent Category III tracing requires obstetric intervention regardless of postpartum contraceptive plans.

Recall
Pregnancy occurs despite a contraceptive method → is termination indicated? What is done?
tap to flip
Answer
No — contraceptive use or failure is not itself a reason for termination.   • ★Barrier and natural methods contain no systemic hormone → no fetal drug exposure if pregnancy occurs; barrier-method use dictates no special interpregnancy interval — base spacing counseling on maternal recovery and reproductive preference.

Board trap · Contraception does not change labor managementContraceptive choice or history has no role in diagnosing active labor, does not alter labor-curve definitions or partogram interpretation, produces no characteristic FHR pattern and does not determine delivery timing in an established pregnancy. A contraceptive-failure pregnancy follows ordinary obstetric labor criteria, and labor abnormalities are managed independently of the planned postpartum method.

Early = 1 shot; late or uncertain = 3 shots; brain or eye = IV.

tap to flip

tap to flip

No — the same penicillin principle applies by stage; for neurosyphilis penicillin remains required.

  • ✎Early syphilis suspected but serology initially negative → repeat at and months.

🎯Tubo-ovarian Abscess (TOA)4 items▾

  • ✎In TOA, pelvic pain is present in about % and fever/leukocytosis in about %; PID progresses to TOA in about %.

Drainage or surgery — indicated for ruptured TOA, peritonitis or failed medical therapy.

🏛️Pelvic Support Levels & Prolapse Staging6 items▾

DeLancey levels of pelvic support
LevelMain supportDefect when damagedAnswer

Recall
Cardinal + uterosacral ligament failure → which prolapse?
tap to flip
Answer
Apical prolapse (uterine or vault) — DeLancey level I.
POP-Q staging (ICS 1996; most distal portion relative to the hymen; TVL = total vaginal length)
StageDefinitionAnswer
0No prolapse — points Aa, Ba, Ap, Bp all at −3 cm; apex at or above −(TVL − 2) cm
IMost distal portion >1 cm above hymen
IIMost distal portion within 1 cm above or below hymen (±1 cm)
IIIMost distal portion >1 cm below hymen, but protruding no further than (TVL − 2) cm
IVComplete eversion — most distal portion protrudes at least (TVL − 2) cm
🧠 Memory toolPOP-Q: the 1-cm rule around the hymen
IAbove the 1-cm zone (>1 cm above hymen)
IIInside the zone (within 1 cm above or below hymen)
IIIBelow the zone (>1 cm below hymen) but not fully out — less than (TVL − 2) cm
IVEverything out — complete eversion, at least (TVL − 2) cm
One landmark (hymen), one number (1 cm): above it, at it, below it, all out. III vs IV is split at total vaginal length minus 2 cm.
Baden-Walker grading (descent relative to the hymen)
GradeDescentAnswer
0Normal position — no descent
1Approximately halfway to hymen
2Reaches hymen
3Approximately halfway beyond hymen

Vaginal inspection, cleaning and replacement of the pessary.

💪Stress Urinary Incontinence: Treatment7 items▾

Recall
First-line treatment of stress urinary incontinence?
tap to flip
Answer
Conservative: weight loss when indicated, caffeine restriction, fluid modification, bladder training, pelvic-floor muscle exercises (Kegels), pelvic-floor physical therapy.
Recall
Nonsurgical alternative for SUI besides exercises?
tap to flip
Answer
An incontinence pessary.
Board trap · A pill for stress incontinenceTempting: pick a drug. Wrong — there is no FDA-approved medication for SUI. Management is conservative, then surgical.
Recall
Definitive / standard operation for persistent SUI after conservative failure?
tap to flip

Midurethral sling, in an appropriate patient.
Recall
Surgical alternatives to the midurethral sling for SUI?
tap to flip
Answer
Burch retropubic suspension or a bladder-neck sling.
Recall
SUI from intrinsic sphincter deficiency → option?
tap to flip

Periurethral / transurethral bulking agent.
🩺 Think it through
After a sling procedure a woman has a weak stream and a post-void residual of 250 mL. What is the problem and what is done?
Postoperative weak stream + high PVR (250 mL is pathologic) = outlet obstruction from overcorrection / the sling — NOT recurrent urgency. If it persists → sling release / revision.

Recall

tap to flip

Behavioral therapy → then an antimuscarinic or a β3-agonist (mirabegron). AUA/SUFU 2024: a strict step-by-step order is no longer required — the drug may be started together with behavioral therapy by shared decision.

DrugDoseRoleAnswer
Oxybutynin5 mg PO BID–TID (maximum 5 mg QID)Antimuscarinic — pharmacologic option after behavioral therapy; counsel on dementia / cognitive risk. Classic textbook: the first-line drug class

Vibegron75 mg dailyβ3-agonist (FDA 2020)

Recall
Antimuscarinics in a patient with dementia?
tap to flip
Answer
Use cautiously — cognitive adverse effects.
Board trap · Mirabegron and blood pressureAVOID mirabegron in severe uncontrolled hypertension (SBP ≥180 and/or DBP ≥110 mmHg; FDA labelling) — check blood pressure before and during treatment. Cardiac arrhythmia is not a labelled contraindication: mirabegron raises heart rate, so it is used with caution in tachyarrhythmia or QT prolongation. Classic textbook: avoid in poorly controlled hypertension or cardiac arrhythmia.
Recall
Urgency UI refractory to behavioral therapy and drugs → three options?
tap to flip

Sacral neuromodulation, percutaneous tibial nerve stimulation, or intradetrusor botulinum toxin.
Recall
Rare, severe, refractory urgency incontinence → operation?
tap to flip

Augmentation cystoplasty.

🚰Overflow, Functional Incontinence & Urinary Fistula6 items▾

Recall
Overflow incontinence from detrusor underactivity → first-line?
tap to flip
Answer
Clean intermittent catheterization.
  • ✎Postsurgical bladder overdistension / retention: temporary continuous bladder drainage for , then reassess.
  • ✎Functional UI, first-line: scheduled / timed toileting — void approximately every .
Recall
Continuous urine leakage within 14 days after pelvic surgery → suspect?
tap to flip
Answer
A urinary fistula — postsurgical fistulas usually become evident within 14 days.
  • ✎Urinary fistula: surgical repair after tissue inflammation subsides — definitive repair of a postsurgical fistula is usually delayed after the injury.
🧠 Memory toolPost-operative urinary timeline
24–48 hTemporary bladder drainage for retention / overdistension
14 daysWindow in which a postsurgical fistula usually declares itself
3–6 monthsUsual delay before definitive fistula repair
Hours → days → months. The same 3–6 months is also the longest interval a pessary may be left between removals.

🤰Prolapse & Incontinence in Pregnancy6 items▾

Recall
Symptomatic pelvic-organ prolapse during pregnancy → management?
tap to flip
Answer
Pessary and follow-up (the conservative option); elective reconstruction is postponed until after delivery.
Board trap · Operating on prolapse or SUI during pregnancyAVOID / defer during pregnancy: elective hysteropexy, uterosacral suspension, midurethral sling, Burch procedure and other reconstructive procedures (sling / Burch / prolapse reconstruction). Prolapse surgery waits until postpartum recovery.
Recall
Stress incontinence arising in pregnancy → management?
tap to flip
Answer
Reassurance / expectant, conservative management — it frequently improves after the peripartum period. No medication, no surgery, no elective sling. If it persists, reassess after postpartum healing.
Board trap · Bladder drugs in pregnancyOxybutynin / other antimuscarinics and mirabegron have no adequate human pregnancy data and no trimester-specific recommendation. Do NOT call them absolutely contraindicated — but they are not recommended in pregnancy and are avoided unless clearly necessary (product labelling); manage with behavioral measures.
Recall
Does prolapse or incontinence change delivery timing?
tap to flip
Answer
No. Prolapse alone → no fixed gestational-age indication for delivery. Stress, urgency, mixed or functional incontinence alone → no change in delivery timing.
Recall
When does prolapse in pregnancy need individualized delivery planning?
tap to flip
Answer
Severe nonreducible prolapse causing true birth-canal obstruction or major urinary obstruction.

StageDefinitionAnswer
IConfined to the cervix
IA1Microscopic only; stromal invasion <3 mm deep
IA2Microscopic only; stromal invasion ≥3 mm and <5 mm deep
IB1Invasion ≥5 mm deep, lesion <2 cm in greatest dimension
IB2Lesion ≥2 cm and <4 cm
IB3Lesion ≥4 cm, still limited to the cervix

IIA2Upper two-thirds of vagina, no parametrial invasion, lesion ≥4 cm

Board trap · FIGO 2018 vs the older cervical stagingOlder tables: IA needed width ≤7 mm, IB was split only at 4 cm (IB1 ≤4 cm, IB2 >4 cm), and nodes did not change the stage. FIGO 2018: horizontal width is no longer counted (depth only); IB is split three ways at 2 cm and 4 cm (IB1/IB2/IB3); any positive node = IIIC (IIIC1 pelvic, IIIC2 para-aortic); imaging and pathology may be used to assign the stage. LVSI is reported but does not change the stage.
Cervical cancer: FIGO 2018 stage → treatment (current guidance, NCCN)
StageHigh-yield treatmentAnswer
IA1 without LVSI, fertility desiredCold-knife cone
IA1 without LVSI, fertility not desiredSimple hysterectomy
IA1 with LVSI, IA2Modified radical hysterectomy + pelvic nodes OR radiation
IB1, IB2, IIA1Radical hysterectomy + pelvic nodes OR radiation
IB3, IIA2 (bulky, ≥4 cm)Cisplatin-based chemoradiation + intracavitary radiation preferred. Classic textbook: radical hysterectomy or radiation for everything through IIA2
IIB–IVACisplatin-based chemoradiation + intracavitary radiation
IVBSystemic platinum-based chemotherapy / palliative care, not curative chemoradiation
Recall
Parametrial invasion → stage and treatment?
tap to flip

Stage IIB → chemoradiation
🩺 Think it through
A woman with stage IA1 cervical cancer, no LVSI, wants future pregnancy. What is the treatment — and what if she did not desire fertility?
Cold-knife cone when fertility is desired; simple hysterectomy when it is not — fertility desire decides, but only in IA1 without LVSI. Board trap: IA1 with LVSI is not treated this way; it is managed like IA2 — modified radical hysterectomy + pelvic nodes OR radiation.

FIGO 2023 endometrial staging — the key changes from FIGO 2009
What changedFIGO 2023Answer
Histology now enters the stageNon-aggressive = low-grade (grade 1–2) endometrioid. Aggressive = grade 3 endometrioid, serous, clear cell, carcinosarcoma, undifferentiated, mixed
Stage I, non-aggressive typesIA1 polyp or endometrium only; IA2 <½ myometrium with no/focal LVSI; IA3 low-grade endometrioid limited to uterus and ovary; IB ≥½ myometrium with no/focal LVSI
Aggressive types confined to the uterusIC if limited to a polyp or the endometrium; IIC with any myometrial invasion
LVSI now enters the stageSubstantial LVSI (≥5 vessels) in a non-aggressive type = IIB; cervical stromal invasion = IIA
Stage III split furtherIIIA1 ovary/tube, IIIA2 serosa; IIIB1 vagina/parametria, IIIB2 pelvic peritoneum; IIIC1 pelvic and IIIC2 para-aortic nodes, each divided into micro- (i) and macrometastasis (ii)
Stage IV now has three partsIVA bladder/bowel mucosa; IVB abdominal peritoneal metastasis beyond the pelvis; IVC distant metastasis
Molecular class may modify early stagePOLE-mutated, stage I–II → IAmPOLEmut (downstaged); p53-abnormal with any myometrial invasion → IICmp53abn (upstaged)
Board trap · Older endometrial staging lettersClassic textbook tables (FIGO 1988) used IA / IB / IC (none / <½ / >½ myometrium) and IIA / IIB (endocervical glands / cervical stroma), and counted positive peritoneal cytology as IIIA. Since FIGO 2009: only IA (<½) and IB (≥½); stage II = cervical stroma only; positive cytology is reported separately and does not change the stage.

🔄Normal Cycle Physiology: the Ovulatory Axis6 items▾

  • ★Normal ovulation sequence: hypothalamic GnRH (pulsatile) → pituitary FSH/LH → follicular development (FSH recruits a dominant follicle) → LH surge → ovulation → corpus-luteum progesterone production. Ovulation requires all three: pulsatile GnRH, FSH recruitment of a dominant follicle, and an LH surge.
Hormonal profile across the menstrual cycle
PhaseDominant hormoneWhat it doesAnswer
Early follicularFSH (rises)Stimulates follicular recruitment and growth
Late follicular (pre-ovulatory)Estradiol from the dominant follicleRises before ovulation and suppresses FSH
MidcycleLH surgeTriggered by estradiol feedback; the surge precedes ovulation (about 36 h after its onset) and so predicts it
LutealProgesterone from the corpus luteumRaises basal body temperature after ovulation
Recall
What triggers the LH surge, and how does the surge relate to ovulation in time?
tap to flip
Answer
Midcycle estradiol feedback triggers the LH surge; the surge comes before ovulation (ovulation follows about 36 h after its onset) — it signals impending ovulation, not ovulation itself.
Recall
Basal body temperature rises after ovulation — which hormone, from where?
tap to flip
Answer
Progesterone from the corpus luteum.
  • ✎Estradiol rising from the dominant follicle suppresses .
🧠 Memory toolOrder of hormone events across the cycle
FFSH — recruits the follicle (early follicular)
EEstradiol — rises from the dominant follicle, suppresses FSH
LLH surge — just before ovulation
PProgesterone — corpus luteum, basal temperature rises
F → E → L → P, in cycle order.

  • ✎Acute progestin regimen: MPA mg TID for days, then 20 mg/day for weeks.
Recall
Ovulatory HMB — the four first-line options?
tap to flip
Answer
NSAID, hormonal contraception, LNG-IUD, or tranexamic acid.
Recall
Chronic anovulation, no fertility desire — why give progestin or an LNG-IUD?
tap to flip
Answer
For endometrial protection (regular progestin exposure).
Recall
Acute nongravid AUB but estrogen is contraindicated (major thrombotic disease) → ?
tap to flip
Answer
High-dose progestin alternative.
Contraindications in menstrual-disorder treatment
Drug / procedureStatusAnswer
Tranexamic acid with active / history of VTECONTRAINDICATED
Tranexamic acid + combined hormonal contraceptionCONTRAINDICATED
High-dose estrogen with major thrombotic diseaseCONTRAINDICATED — use the progestin alternative
Endometrial ablation when future pregnancy / fertility is desiredCONTRAINDICATED — pregnancy afterward is unsafe / high risk
Board trap · Tranexamic acidTempting: add tranexamic acid for HMB in any patient. Right: it is CONTRAINDICATED with active or past thromboembolism (VTE) and together with combined hormonal contraception (CHC).
Board trap · Estrogen before pregnancy is excludedTempting: start high-dose estrogen for heavy bleeding straight away. Right: it is nongravid therapy only — do not use it before pregnancy is excluded, and evaluate unexplained vaginal bleeding first; do not give estrogen empirically.
  • ★Delivery timing in a later pregnancy: prior amenorrhea / AUB / polyp / benign hyperplasia → no disease-specific delivery timing; prior uncomplicated hysteroscopic polypectomy → no routine delivery-timing change.

🔬Who Needs Endometrial Sampling5 items▾

Endometrial biopsy: cut-offs and intervals
SituationActionAnswer
AUB at age >45 yr (ACOG 2012)Endometrial biopsy at presentation
Younger AUB + major endometrial-cancer riskEndometrial biopsy regardless of age
Postmenopausal bleeding + endometrial stripe >4 mm (ACOG 2018)Endometrial sampling; a stripe ≤4 mm is reassuring (cancer risk <1%)
Persistent / recurrent postmenopausal bleedingEMB / hysteroscopy even after a reassuring initial study
Tamoxifen without bleedingNo routine endometrial screening
Tamoxifen + abnormal bleedingInvestigate immediately
  • ✎AUB at age over years (ACOG 2012) → endometrial biopsy at presentation; with significant endometrial-cancer risk, biopsy earlier, regardless of age.
  • ✎Postmenopausal bleeding with an endometrial stripe greater than mm → endometrial sampling; mm is reassuring (ACOG 2018).
Recall
Tamoxifen: bleeding vs no bleeding — what is done?
tap to flip
Answer
No bleeding: no routine endometrial screening.
Abnormal bleeding: investigate immediately — endometrial evaluation required.
🧠 Memory toolTriggers for tissue diagnosis
45AUB above this age → EMB
RiskMajor endometrial-cancer risk → EMB at any age
4 mmPostmenopausal bleeding with a stripe above this (≤4 mm is reassuring)
AgainPersistent / recurrent postmenopausal bleeding → sample even after a reassuring study

⚠️Endometrial Hyperplasia & EIN8 items▾

Endometrial hyperplasia: two-tier classification (WHO 2014, retained 2020) and cancer risk
CategoryCytologic atypiaRiskAnswer
Hyperplasia without atypia (benign; replaces simple and complex hyperplasia without atypia)AbsentProgression to cancer <5% over 20 yr (RCOG 2016)
Atypical hyperplasia / EIN (endometrial intraepithelial neoplasia; replaces simple and complex atypical hyperplasia)Present — premalignantCoexistent carcinoma in about 30%–50% at hysterectomy (ACOG 2023); classic textbook figure 27%–52% coexistent / progression risk
🧠 Memory toolClassic textbook four-tier hyperplasia risk ladder (older WHO 1994 scheme)
1Simple, no atypia — 1%
3Complex, no atypia — 3%
8Simple atypical — 8%
29Complex atypical — 29%
1 – 3 – 8 – 29: atypia is the big jump. This four-tier scheme is superseded; today the first two are reported as hyperplasia without atypia and the last two as atypical hyperplasia / EIN.
  • ✎Atypical hyperplasia / EIN: coexistent carcinoma in about of hysterectomy specimens (ACOG 2023); hyperplasia without atypia progresses in under % over 20 years.
  • ✎Benign hyperplasia without atypia — FIRST-LINE: progestin for months, then repeat .
Recall
EIN diagnosed on EMB — what next before definitive treatment, and why?
tap to flip
Answer
Hysteroscopy + D&C to exclude coexistent carcinoma.
Recall
EIN, fertility desired — alternative, and the resampling schedule?
tap to flip
Answer
High-dose progestin + strict serial sampling: first resampling at 3 mo, then at least every 6 mo.
Board trap · EIN: definitive vs unacceptable treatmentEIN with fertility complete → FIRST-LINE definitive: total hysterectomy. Tempting but not acceptable for EIN: endometrial ablation (CONTRAINDICATED), supracervical hysterectomy and power morcellation.
🩺 Think it through
A woman who has completed childbearing has EIN on endometrial biopsy. What is done to complete the evaluation, and what is the definitive treatment?
Hysteroscopy + D&C to exclude coexistent carcinoma (about 30%–50% risk), then total hysterectomy — not ablation, supracervical hysterectomy or power morcellation.

🔍Breast Mass Work-up & BI-RADS7 items▾

Recall
Breast mass, age <30 yr → first imaging?
tap to flip
Answer
Ultrasound first.
Recall
Breast mass, age ≥30 yr → imaging?
tap to flip

Diagnostic mammography ± targeted ultrasound.
BI-RADS categories — meaning and management (ACR BI-RADS 5th ed.)
BI-RADSMeaningManagementAnswer
0IncompleteAdditional imaging
1NegativeRoutine screening
2BenignRoutine screening
3Probably benign (≤2% likelihood of malignancy)Short-interval (6-month) imaging follow-up
4Suspicious (>2% to <95%) — 4A low >2% to ≤10%; 4B moderate >10% to ≤50%; 4C high >50% to <95%Biopsy
5Highly suggestive of malignancy (≥95%)Biopsy / oncologic evaluation
6Known biopsy-proven malignancyTreatment planning
Board trap · BI-RADS 4–5 is not a screening categoryTempting: keep the patient on routine screening or interval follow-up. Right: BI-RADS 4 or 5 → biopsy; interval follow-up belongs to BI-RADS 3 only.
Board trap · Normal mammogram, palpable lesionA suspicious palpable lesion is NOT excluded by a normal mammogram.

tap to flip

>1 cm, fixed, irregular, firm, or multiple.

tap to flip

Breast cancer screening by group (current guidance)
GroupRecommendationAnswer
Mammography, average risk — startAge 40 (USPSTF 2024; ACOG 2024)
Mammography, average risk — intervalUSPSTF 2024: every 2 yr, age 40–74. ACOG 2024: every 1 or 2 yr by shared decision
Philippine standardPhilHealth 2025 screening standards: mammogram every 2 yr at 40–69 yr; clinical breast exam for all women from age 25

🛡️Sexual Assault & Intimate Partner Violence3 items▾

Sexual assault — time windows
IssueWindow / ruleAnswer
HIV PEPStart as soon as possible, no later than 72 h after exposure; 28-day course (CDC 2025)
Forensic evidence collectionAs soon as possible; many current protocols collect up to 120 h (5 days) (US NIJ 2017), varying by jurisdiction. Classic textbook: ≤96 h
Emergency contraceptionOffer up to 120 h (5 days) (ACOG 2015): copper IUD is most effective; ulipristal acetate 30 mg is more effective than levonorgestrel and keeps its efficacy to 120 h; levonorgestrel 1.5 mg works best ≤72 h (labelled window), with efficacy falling toward 120 h. Classic textbook: levonorgestrel 1.5 mg ≤120 h
Follow-up / reassessment1–4 wk
🧠 Memory toolSexual-assault clocks
72 hHIV PEP must start by now; levonorgestrel 1.5 mg works best within this window
120 hOuter limit for emergency contraception (ulipristal, copper IUD); forensic evidence in many current protocols
1–4 wkFollow-up visit
Number hook: 3 days → 5 days → 1–4 weeks.
  • ★IPV approach: screen/recognize → safety assessment → documentation → referral/resources → ongoing reassessment.
